daily.title: Malaysia's middle path between China and US faces new tests
daily.summary: The prime minister's comments on Taiwan and US-backed military facilities near Sabah have revived questions over Malaysia's non-aligned foreign policy.

daily.title: Iran bets on shadow networks to evade US sanctions
daily.summary: To circumvent US sanctions, Iran has spent decades building a complex network of businesspeople and companies. A billionaire once sentenced to death is now back at its center.

daily.title: India news: Jaishankar offers help to end war in Ukraine
daily.summary: Foreign Minister S. Jaishankar says India is prepared to assist efforts to end the war in Ukraine, as the foreign minister visits Kyiv. DW has more.

daily.title: Gloria Steinem, feminist activist and journalist, dies at 92
daily.summary: Steinem became a prominent leader of the second wave of the feminist movement in the US.

daily.title: 'Supersized' El Nino could be strongest on record, UN says
daily.summary: The current El Nino could end up being the strongest since records began 40 years ago, the UN warns. It says the phenomenon is being "supersized" thanks to exceptionally warm temperatures in the tropical Pacific Ocean.

daily.title: Data centers are everywhere. Here's what they're doing to the planet.
daily.summary: As data centers multiply to meet AI demand, they're straining power grids, draining water supplies, and reshaping the land and air around them.

daily.title: Germany news: Police say arson attack targeted defense firm
daily.summary: Two people were arrested in connection with a small fire at a construction site near a technology and defense company in Munich. Investigators are looking at a possible "political motive." More on DW.

daily.title: US, Australia to boost defense ties amid China's growing influence
daily.summary: The two countries said they had agreed to speed up cooperation and boost US military presence in Australia to counter China's unprecedented military buildup.

daily.title: US: New York City Mayor Mamdani announces ban on AI for younger students
daily.summary: New York City is barring elementary and middle school students from using generative AI tools this school year. Meanwhile AI literacy classes and supervised pilot programs will be rolled out for high schoolers.

daily.title: Russia to close branches of Germany's Goethe-Institut
daily.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said the move was in response to Germany's decision to close the Russian House in Berlin after blaming Moscow for an attemped drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport.

daily.title: US: 3 dead including suspect in Minneapolis shooting
daily.summary: The motive for the shooting is still unclear. Local authorities and the FBI are responding to the incident.

daily.title: UNICEF: 1 in 5 youths targeted by online sexual abuse
daily.summary: A survey of around 21,000 young people by the UN's agency for children has found that online sexual abuse of minors is on the rise.

daily.title: Spain: Tens of thousands rally over Ceuta crisis
daily.summary: Tensions continue over migrants still stranded in Ceuta and the Sanchez government’s handling of the fallout.

daily.title: Malta: Businessman acquitted of journalist's murder
daily.summary: Yorgen Fenech was suspected to have masterminded the murder of investigative journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia, whose family continue to demand justice for her killing.

daily.title: Berlin's punitive measures unlikely to deter Putin: experts
daily.summary: Germany has announced punitive measures after publicly blaming Russia for an attempted airport drone attack. But a former diplomat, political and security analysts warn it will likely do little to deter the Kremlin.

daily.title: Is Libya's damaging power struggle about to end?
daily.summary: The North African country has been divided between two rival governments for more than a decade. Countrywide elections could finally end the split and reunite Libya.

daily.title: Germany: How to woo voters with an immigrant background
daily.summary: The number of voters in Germany with an immigrant background is rising. Yet the established parties barely manage to reach them. Why not?

daily.title: Macron visits Bayeux Tapestry with King Charles, PM Andy Burnham
daily.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron is on a shorter-term visit to the UK than the renowned on-loan 11th century tapestry. He viewed the ancient artwork with the UK monarch and relatively new Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

daily.title: Russia's hybrid attacks on Germany: When is it 'war?'
daily.summary: The German government is holding Russia responsible for an unsuccessful attack in Leipzig. Yet many feel that its response has been too mild.

daily.title: Austria women ice hockey team fight for future generations
daily.summary: Austria are getting ready for their first Women's Ice Hockey World Championship. But preparations have been overshadowed by a dispute about conditions, pay and getting men's cast-off kit. A solution now looks in sight.

weekly.title: EU summons Russian envoy over failed Leipzig drone attack
weekly.summary: The EU's foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said the attempted attack had "all the hallmarks of state-sponsored terrorism." She said the EU was summoning a Russian envoy, with France announcing a similar step.

weekly.title: Women's football: Anyomi, London City and the German exodus
weekly.summary: Nicole Anyomi has joined Alexia Putellas and other star names in signing for the ambitious English club London City Lionesses. The Germany winger told DW England is a better place to develop her game than back home.

weekly.title: Ukraine: Russia threatens 'devastating' Baltic response
weekly.summary: Any escalation in the Baltic region will lead to a significant response, Moscow said.

weekly.title: Germany says Russia behind attempted drone attack at Leipzig airport
weekly.summary: Investigators believe an explosives-laden drone was deliberately targeting a Ukrainian cargo aircraft at Leipzig/Halle airport in early August. The German government said on Tuesday that it held Russia "responsible."

weekly.title: Germany terminates lease for Berlin's Russian House
weekly.summary: Germany has announced the termination of the lease for the Russian House in the heart of Berlin. Critics have long said it is a hub for propaganda and espionage.

weekly.title: Can communities be proteced from melting glaciers?
weekly.summary: Rising temperatures are increasing the risk of floods and avalanches in mountain regions. The disaster in Nepal and Tibet shows the urgent need for solutions, and the tools that could help save lives.

weekly.title: Mladic's death, Bosnia and Serbia's unfinished reckoning
weekly.summary: The death of Ratko Mladic did not close a dark chapter of European history; it reopened old wounds. The ideology that created him lives on. The Dayton peace agreement ended the war, not the divisions that produced it.

weekly.title: Norway's new King Haakon VIII takes oath in parliament
weekly.summary: The new king swore to uphold the constitution in parliament in Oslo, the first major institutional step of his reign. Haakon VIII's wife Queen Mette-Marit had to skip the event in the aftermath of her lung transplant.

weekly.title: Germany's center-left SPD is fighting for survival
weekly.summary: The Social Democratic Party is sinking ever deeper into crisis. Voters are turning away, while unrest is growing within its grassroots ranks. Will upcoming state elections accelerate the party's downward spiral?

weekly.title: US irks Germany, Europe with Russian G20 invite, press bans
weekly.summary: Russia's finance minister is at the G20 meeting in Asheville but some key US press corps members are not. The mood was already tense amid the lengthy Iran war and Trump's renewed beef with neighbor Canada.

weekly.title: Can new Apple CEO John Ternus fix the tech giant's AI woes?
weekly.summary: John Ternus is just the third Apple CEO in 30 years. His primary challenge is to correct the company's faltering AI strategy to preserve its position as a big tech leader.

weekly.title: Ulrich Siegmund wants to make Saxony-Anhalt a model for AfD rule
weekly.summary: The AfD's lead candidate Ulrich Siegmund aims to turn his small federal state into a blueprint for right-wing extremist politics across Germany.

weekly.title: At Venice Film Festival, politics take center stage
weekly.summary: With works about Gaza, Ukraine and Elon Musk, political cinema is in the spotlight at the 2026 Venice Film Festival.

weekly.title: Canada's Carney holds firm against Trump tariffs
weekly.summary: Canada is facing new US import penalties after Prime Minister Mark Carney refused to match US tariffs on China. Other countries are watching as the Trump trade clash turns into a fight over economic sovereignty.

weekly.title: Saxony-Anhalt State Premier Schulze takes on far-right AfD
weekly.summary: The AfD is far ahead in the polls in Saxony-Anhalt. But Schulze is determined to keep the AfD from becoming the first far-right party since World War II to lead a German state government.

weekly.title: Inside the sea cucumber smuggling boom
weekly.summary: A quiet multimillion‑dollar black market is exploding across the Indian Ocean, driven by one unlikely animal: the sea cucumber.

weekly.title: Ailing Djokovic 'despised' every moment of US Open defeat
weekly.summary: Novak Djokovic has exited in the first round of a Grand Slam for the first time in over two decades. Could time — or an unknown health condition — be catching up with the Serbian tennis legend?

weekly.title: Germany news: Summer was 2nd hottest of the century — DWD
weekly.summary: Germany's DWD weather service says the summer was second only to 2003 in terms of average temperatures. It was also unusually dry. In Cologne, police are seeking a man who fired shots at a cafe storefront.

weekly.title: Fact check: Germany's Merz misstates record in ARD interview
weekly.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz made several misleading claims on migration, debt and electric vehicles in his summer interview with German public broadcaster ARD.

weekly.title: German churches speak out against AfD ahead of state election
weekly.summary: As the far-right AfD party leads the polls ahead of Sunday's election in Saxony-Anhalt, church leaders have warned against downplaying its "ethnonationalist" agenda.

weekly.title: EU wants drones to spray pesticides, but it could backfire
weekly.summary: The EU wants to lift a decades-old ban on spraying pesticides from the air, allowing drones to be used for greater precision. But experts warn the plan could lead to even more pesticides being used in agriculture.

weekly.title: Greece, Turkey clash over protected Aegean marine areas
weekly.summary: Turkey has announced the creation of two protected zones in a disputed area of the Aegean Sea, sparking an angry reaction from Greece. Does this mark a new chapter in a long-running dispute between the two countries?

weekly.title: Russian-American heads Trump's planned Caucasus trade route
weekly.summary: A Russian-born businessman heads the investment fund financing the so-called "Trump Route," a planned corridor through Armenia linking Azerbaijan with Nakhchivan. Who is Konstantin Sokolov, and what role does he play?

weekly.title: Saxony-Anhalt election: Why the AfD is so strong
weekly.summary: The AfD is polling above 40% ahead of Saxony-Anhalt's election on September 6. What is driving support for the far right in this predominantly rural eastern German state?

weekly.title: This extremely successful author polarizes German readers
weekly.summary: She's young and she says what she thinks: Caroline Wahl is topping Germany's bestseller lists with her novels. But she has also faced a public backlash.

weekly.title: Serbia keeps EU, Russia in play ahead of key election
weekly.summary: As Serbia heads toward an uncertain election, President Aleksandar Vucic is balancing ties with Russia and EU ambitions. But growing geopolitical tensions and pressure at home are narrowing his room to maneuver.

weekly.title: What 'The Odyssey' can teach us about climate chaos
weekly.summary: The Bronze Age collapse may have started with a water crisis. The droughts of today raise the unsettling question of whether it could happen again.

weekly.title: Influential humanists: These are the winners of the Goethe Medal 2026
weekly.summary: The prestigious German cultural award recognizes the artistic work and commitment to cultural dialogue of Arvo Pärt, Anita Raja and Prodromos Tsinikoris.

weekly.title: Germany's military wants to recruit tech-savvy gamers
weekly.summary: The Bundeswehr has been a fixture at Gamescom, Cologne's video game trade fair, for years. But critics say military recruitment does not belong at an entertainment convention.

weekly.title: Norway's King Harald dies at 89
weekly.summary: King Harald is succeeded by his son, who has taken the name King Haakon VIII, with Crown Princess Mette-Marit now queen.

weekly.title: Protesters set fire to migrant camp in Ceuta
weekly.summary: The unrest comes one month after a mass influx of migrants from Morocco to the Spanish exclave in North Africa.

weekly.title: Spain: Thieves steal Bronze Age gold in lightning raid on Villena Museum
weekly.summary: One of the world's greatest Bronze Age gold collections has been swiped, almost in its entirety, from Villena Museum. A highly professional group of thieves were in and out in four minutes flat before the museum opened.

weekly.title: Ratko Mladic, the man behind Srebrenica massacre, dies at 84
weekly.summary: For many, Ratko Mladic represented the horrors of the Bosnian war. He was convicted of genocide for the Srebrenica massacre and other war crimes. On Thursday, he died in detention at The Hague.

weekly.title: Tragedy in Nepal: How do flash floods happen?
weekly.summary: When flash floods sweep through the Himalayas, there is often little time to react. Scientists are working to understand the risks and improve early warning systems.

weekly.title: Andre Rankel named Germany's new men's ice hockey coach
weekly.summary: Germany's men's ice hockey team has appointed a new head coach following a string of dissappointing tournaments. He's two decades younger than the man he's replacing but he has no previous experience as a head coach.

weekly.title: New study shows German football remains male-dominated
weekly.summary: The top leagues of German football remain a largely male environment. A new study reveals that only seven clubs have women in upper management levels.

weekly.title: Ex-Bosnian Serb military leader Ratko Mladic dead at 84
weekly.summary: The former Bosnian Serb general was convicted of genocide committed during the bloody 1992-95 war in Bosnia and Herzegovina.
